steps.title: Lysis and Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Isolate RNA from cell lines using TRIZOL and chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of TRIZOL for RNA isolation.
Add 200 µL of chloroform and shake vigorously for 15 seconds.
Incubate for 3-10 min at room temperature (RT) to allow for phase separation.

steps.title: Centrifuge and Collect Aqueous Phase
steps.instruction: Separate the phases via centrifugation and recover the RNA-containing layer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge for 15 minutes at maximum speed and 4 °C (Note: for tissue samples, spinning for 20 minutes can help remove 'white floaties' from the aqueous phase).
Carefully collect 3/4 of the upper aqueous phase.
Mix the collected aqueous phase with an equal volume of cold 100% isopropanol (e.g., 500 μL).
Optional: Add 7 µL of acrylamide if a low amount of RNA is expected (typically not needed for 6-well plates or larger).

Incubate for 10 minutes at RT, or longer at -20 °C (if expecting low yield, leave overnight at -20 °C). Note: For tissue samples, do not let RNA precipitate for longer than 10 min; centrifuge step can usually start right away.

steps.title: Pellet Recovery and Washing
steps.instruction: Recover the RNA pellet and wash to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge for 15 minutes at maximum speed and 4 °C.
Wash the pellet with 1 mL of cold 75% (or 70%) EtOH.
Vortex or pipette the sample briefly to ensure the pellet is completely washed.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at maximum speed and 4 °C.

steps.title: EtOH Removal and Drying
steps.instruction: Remove all residual ethanol and dry the RNA pellet.

substeps.instruction: Remove the supernatant by dumping into a waste container, draining onto a paper towel, and spinning tubes down in a microfuge.
Dry the pellet for approximately 10-20 minutes (e.g., upside down on a Kimwipe or on the air-intake of the hood).

steps.title: Resuspension and Incubation
steps.instruction: Resuspend the RNA pellet in water and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 15 µL of dH2O (Note: for tissue samples, resuspend in 50-60 µL of dH2O).
